rule.title: Delete Volume Shadow Copies Via WMI With PowerShell
rule.author: frack113

es.summary: Un motor de PowerShell se inició con una línea de comandos que consulta Win32_ShadowCopy mediante Get-WmiObject y la borra con Delete() o Remove-WmiObject. Es un patrón típico de ransomware antes del cifrado.
es.what_it_detects: Eventos 400 del log clásico de Windows PowerShell (ps_classic_start) cuyo campo Data, donde está HostApplication, contiene a la vez 'Get-WmiObject' y 'Win32_ShadowCopy', además de 'Delete()' o 'Remove-WmiObject'.
es.why_it_matters: Borrar las instantáneas de volumen (Volume Shadow Copies) impide restaurar archivos y versiones previas. Corresponde a ATT&CK T1490, Inhibit System Recovery, y suele preceder al cifrado masivo o a una acción destructiva.
triage_steps: Lea el campo Data completo: HostApplication muestra la línea de comandos exacta, y EngineVersion indica si se usó PowerShell 2.0 para evadir el registro.
Identifique el host (Computer) y el usuario que ejecutó el proceso; confirme si es una cuenta administrativa conocida y si el cambio estaba autorizado.
Revise la telemetría de procesos del host en una ventana de +/- 15 minutos para ver el proceso padre (cmd, wscript, wmiprvse, psexesvc o un binario desconocido).
Busque en el mismo host otros métodos de recuperación inhibida: vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit /set recoveryenabled no o wbadmin delete catalog.
Busque señales de cifrado: renombrado masivo de archivos, notas de rescate, picos de escritura en disco o detención de servicios de backup y bases de datos.
Correlacione al mismo usuario y origen de sesión con otros hosts: logons remotos, ejecución vía WinRM/PsExec o alertas previas de movimiento lateral.
Revise alertas previas de la misma entidad: volcado de credenciales, desactivación del antivirus o herramientas de acceso remoto.
false_positives: Un administrador borra instantáneas antiguas para liberar espacio en disco, siguiendo una solicitud de cambio documentada.
Scripts de mantenimiento o de software de backup que rotan instantáneas mediante WMI, ejecutados desde cuentas de servicio conocidas.
Pruebas de Atomic Red Team o ejercicios de red team autorizados (T1490).
response_steps: Confirme con el propietario del host o el equipo de TI si la ejecución fue legítima; si no lo es, escale como posible incidente de ransomware.
Aísle el endpoint desde el EDR para frenar el cifrado y la propagación, y conserve la memoria y los logs antes de reiniciar.
Deshabilite o restablezca las credenciales de la cuenta implicada y revise sus sesiones activas en otros hosts.
Identifique y elimine el payload y los mecanismos de persistencia, y bloquee sus hashes en toda la flota.
Restaure desde backups fuera de línea verificados y confirme que las instantáneas y la protección del sistema vuelvan a funcionar.
es.severity_rationale: El nivel high se justifica porque borrar instantáneas por WMI rara vez es legítimo y suele indicar una etapa de ransomware en curso.

en.summary: A PowerShell engine started with a command line that queries Win32_ShadowCopy via Get-WmiObject and deletes it with Delete() or Remove-WmiObject. This is a common ransomware step before encryption.
en.what_it_detects: Classic Windows PowerShell log event 400 (ps_classic_start) whose Data field, which holds HostApplication, contains both 'Get-WmiObject' and 'Win32_ShadowCopy' plus either 'Delete()' or 'Remove-WmiObject'.
en.why_it_matters: Deleting Volume Shadow Copies removes restore points and previous file versions. This maps to ATT&CK T1490, Inhibit System Recovery, and usually comes before mass encryption or destructive activity.
triage_steps: Read the full Data field: HostApplication shows the exact command line, and EngineVersion shows whether PowerShell 2.0 was used to evade logging.
Identify the host (Computer) and the executing user; check whether it is a known admin account and whether an approved change exists.
Review process telemetry on the host within +/- 15 minutes to find the parent process (cmd, wscript, wmiprvse, psexesvc or an unknown binary).
Hunt the same host for other recovery inhibition: vssadmin delete shadows, wmic shadowcopy delete, bcdedit recoveryenabled no, wbadmin delete catalog.
Look for encryption signs: mass file renames, ransom notes, disk write spikes, or backup and database services being stopped.
Pivot on the same user and logon source across other hosts: remote logons, WinRM/PsExec execution, earlier lateral movement alerts.
Check earlier alerts for the same entity: credential dumping, antivirus tampering or remote access tools.
false_positives: An administrator removes old shadow copies to free disk space under a documented change request.
Maintenance scripts or backup software rotating shadow copies via WMI from known service accounts.
Atomic Red Team tests or authorized red team exercises for T1490.
response_steps: Confirm with the host owner or IT whether the run was legitimate; if not, escalate as a suspected ransomware incident.
Isolate the endpoint via EDR to stop encryption and spread, and preserve memory and logs before any reboot.
Disable or reset the involved account's credentials and review its active sessions on other hosts.
Find and remove the payload and persistence, and block its hashes fleet-wide.
Restore from verified offline backups and confirm shadow copies and system protection work again.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because deleting shadow copies via WMI is rarely legitimate and usually signals an active ransomware stage.

positive.description: PowerShell iterates Win32_ShadowCopy objects and calls Delete() on each one

event.Data: Available None 	NewEngineState=Available PreviousEngineState=None SequenceNumber=13 HostName=ConsoleHost HostVersion=5.1.19041.1 EngineVersion=5.1.19041.1 RunspaceId=3f2a1c9e-7b41-4c1e-9d2a-0b8e5f6a7c11 HostApplication=powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -Command "Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy | ForEach-Object {$_.Delete();}"

positive.description: PowerShell 2.0 engine pipes Win32_ShadowCopy objects to Remove-WmiObject

event.Data: Available None 	NewEngineState=Available PreviousEngineState=None SequenceNumber=9 HostName=ConsoleHost HostVersion=2.0 EngineVersion=2.0 HostApplication=C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -Version 2 -Command Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_ShadowCopy | Remove-WmiObject

negative.description: Administrator only lists shadow copies with Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy, without deleting them

event.Data: Available None 	NewEngineState=Available PreviousEngineState=None SequenceNumber=15 HostName=ConsoleHost HostVersion=5.1.17763.1 EngineVersion=5.1.17763.1 HostApplication=powershell.exe -Command "Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy | Select-Object ID, InstallDate, VolumeName"

negative.description: Script deletes a WMI object with Remove-WmiObject, but it targets a process, not Win32_ShadowCopy

event.Data: Available None 	NewEngineState=Available PreviousEngineState=None SequenceNumber=21 HostName=ConsoleHost HostVersion=5.1.19041.1 EngineVersion=5.1.19041.1 HostApplication=powershell.exe -Command "Get-WmiObject Win32_Process -Filter \"Name='notepad.exe'\" | Remove-WmiObject"
